clue.text: "The hold is loaded to capacity, Admiral"

parts.note: something loaded to capacity is full
Horatio Nelson, Britain's most famous admiral

explanation.surface: A cargo hold is crammed full, someone reports to the admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hold' reads like a ship's hold to go with the admiral, but it is a wrestling hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip in which both arms lock behind an opponent's neck is the most famous such hold.

clue.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer shoring up Johnson Sr's position

indicators.note: in a down entry, propping something up from below puts these letters underneath the other piece

parts.note: Stanley Johnson, father of the former Prime Minister Boris Johnson, is Stan for short
CE is an abbreviation for Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister

explanation.surface: The finance minister props up the political position of Boris Johnson's father.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'shoring up' puts CE beneath STAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the position or attitude someone takes on an issue.

clue.text: Early consumers of 7 — with reservations

parts.note: 7 down is the bison, eaten by the Plains peoples before settlers came; 'with reservations' looks like doubt but means the lands set aside for these peoples

explanation.surface: Diners who tried bison early on, though with some doubts about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With reservations' reads as hesitancy or as a restaurant booking; it means the reservations of land in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous peoples of the American plains hunted and ate bison long before settlers, and many later lived on reservations.

clue.text: Chap right out of flatfish

indicators.note: the right abbreviation is taken out of the fish's name, leaving the rest

parts.note: the brill is a European flatfish

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to his share of the flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' takes R from BRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill is a common man's name, and a chap is any man.

clue.text: Female runs American Corporation, part of a solid foundation

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, as is tum

explanation.surface: A woman heads an American company that supplies part of a firm's solid base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but means a paunch, giving TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone or pyramid with its top sliced off leaves a truncated solid, the shape used for many plinths and bases.

clue.text: Office plods every now and again lost discipline

indicators.note: letters of the two words are dropped one after another, keeping only every other one

explanation.surface: Office drudges who now and then lose their self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on of OFFICE PLODS keeps the second, fourth and onward.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study, such as physics or law, is an academic discipline.

clue.text: Attempt to hide a pound in hat?

indicators.note: the attempt word hides the other letters inside itself

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a means one, the Roman numeral I
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stash a pound coin inside a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and an indented crown.

clue.text: After extra time upset, wins cup after cup from them?

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read from the bottom

parts.note: AET, short for after extra time, is printed beside football results decided in extra time
to bag something is to win or secure it

explanation.surface: A football side, beaten after extra time, still wins cup after cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AET into TEA. AET is a football scoring convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sachet of tea can be brewed for one cup after another, so these are the source of many cups.

clue.text: Rebuff a loathsome, grasping, beastly individual

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, as if gripping it

explanation.surface: Turn away a horrible, greedy, brutish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping' looks like part of the description of the person; it signals letters held across Rebuff a loathsome.
explanation.definitionFit: A bison is a single beast, so a beastly individual is a playful way of saying one animal.

clue.text: Healthy 18D

definitions.meaning: healthy means in good health, not ill
18 down is a natural source of water, as is a dug shaft for water

explanation.definitionFit: Someone healthy is fit and fine, and a water source from the ground is either of the two words.

clue.text: Shoot a film with Loren — not as good as La Dolce Vita

definitions.text: not as good as La Dolce Vita

indicators.note: shooting a film is the surface, but shoot here means the letters are fired off into a new order

explanation.surface: Make a movie with Sophia Loren — though it won't match Fellini's La Dolce Vita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' rearranges A FILM and LOREN. La Dolce Vita is Fellini's film; its title means 'the sweet life'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet life is a life of luxury, so ordinary everyday living falls short of it.

clue.text: Stick 4 in this place?

parts.note: 4 down's answer, a bill, can be an advertisement, an ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to stick a poster just here.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is BILL, a poster or advert; AD is the cross-reference's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: Minnelli's debut in Cabaret edited — it needs dressing

indicators.note: edited means the letters are reworked and reordered
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Liza Minnelli's first film role in Cabaret was cut, and the costume needs work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debut' takes M from Minnelli; 'edited' rearranges it with CABARET. Liza Minnelli starred in the film Cabaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed crab is a classic dish, so the shellfish flesh is what gets dressed with seasoning.

clue.text: Mr Fitzgerald eating an ounce South Africa cheese

indicators.note: the title takes the other letters inside itself, as if eating them

parts.note: taken as written
oz is the abbreviation for an ounce
ZA is the international code for South Africa
Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A man called Fitzgerald eats an ounce of South African cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Fitzgerald' reads as one man, but it is split: the title is cut open, and the jazz singer's first name follows. ZA is South Africa's international code.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozzarella is a soft white Italian cheese, traditionally made from buffalo milk.

clue.text: Oxford's current fertility goddess

definitions.meaning: the stretch of the River Thames through Oxford has its own name, so it is Oxford's flowing water
the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and fertility

explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford is locally called by the Egyptian goddess's name, and she was worshipped for fertility and magic.

clue.text: Flogged one Queen's Guardsman?

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell
one is the Roman numeral I
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A royal guard was whipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' looks like a beating; it is British slang for sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardsman is an example of a serving soldier, hence the question mark.

clue.text: New hairpieces covering Beatle's group

indicators.note: the hairpieces cover the other letter by surrounding it

parts.note: wigs are hairpieces

explanation.surface: Fresh wigs to cover the mop tops of a Beatle's band.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney formed the band Wings after the Beatles split.

clue.text: Holyrood's call to get rid of moderate politicians in surfer gear?

indicators.note: Holyrood is the Scottish Parliament, so the cry is spoken in a Scottish accent

parts.words: to get rid of moderate politicians
parts.note: wets are moderate Conservatives in Thatcher's day; a call to get rid of them is 'wets out', which a Scot says as wets oot

explanation.surface: The Scottish Parliament demands the moderates be thrown out, dressed as surfers.
explanation.walkthrough: WETS was Thatcher's name for moderate Tories; in Scots 'out' is 'oot', so 'Wets oot!' is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfers wear a close-fitting rubber suit to keep warm in cold water.

clue.text: Unknown character reflecting low buzzing sound

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure gives off a low hum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' turns MOO into OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoom imitates the buzz of something speeding past, an onomatopoeic word.

clue.text: Seafood board not for turning

parts.note: a plank is a board

indicators.note: the word is offered up for turning, so its letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A seafood platter that cannot be turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For turning' reverses NOT to make TON; it echoes Thatcher's 'The lady's not for turning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms are food in the sea for whales and fish, hence a playful seafood.

clue.text: Boombastic singer's retiring to eat a horse

definitions.note: the singer of the 1995 hit Boombastic, with the 's read as is

indicators.note: the shy word takes the other letters inside, as if eating them

parts.note: retiring means shy
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, GG

explanation.surface: A pop singer withdraws to go and eat horsemeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jamaican-American reggae artist who sang Boombastic performs under this stage name.

clue.text: Jump a season?

definitions.meaning: one of the four seasons, between winter and summer

explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to bound up, and the blossoming season after winter shares the same word.

clue.text: Misses US Army man Stevenson

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island, signed as RLS

explanation.surface: A US soldier named Stevenson fails to hit the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' looks like a verb; it is the plural of Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Misses are young unmarried women, addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Jack (Knut's parcel deliveryman) was famous for his service

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
Knut is the setter, so Knut's means the setter is: I'm
a courier delivers parcels

explanation.surface: Jack, the setter's delivery driver, was known for good service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like delivery work; it is the tennis serve of the American world number one of the early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tennis player won four Grand Slam titles and was renowned for his powerful serve.

clue.text: Workplace offering the daily grind

parts.note: the daily grind looks like dull routine work, but here coffee beans are ground every day

explanation.surface: An office where the same tedious work goes on every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee shop grinds beans each day, and many people work there on laptops.

clue.text: Hard cash reguerdon paid out on a regular basis

indicators.text: paid out on a regular basis
indicators.note: letters are let go at regular intervals, keeping every second one

explanation.surface: A reward in hard cash handed over at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Reguerdon is an archaic word for a reward; its second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency is hard cash in the sense of solid, stable money.

clue.text: Positive result for Formula One team's head

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
F1 is Formula One, with the 1 as I

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A good outcome for the boss of a Formula One racing team.
explanation.definitionFit: Making money is a positive financial result, gain over costs.

clue.text: Confound Gainsbourg and Birkin's work, in the end

indicators.note: only the closing words of the song title are kept, dropping its start

parts.note: Serge Gainsbourg and Jane Birkin recorded the 1969 hit Je t'aime... moi non plus

explanation.surface: Puzzle over the meaning of Gainsbourg and Birkin's famous song, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' drops JE T'AIME MOI from the start of the song title.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or perplex someone so they cannot respond is a synonym.
